F4 falsely promotes every balanced pairing to an R-linear map: conjugation of zw over C is balanced but not C-linear. This is nonfatal to the algebra claim, since its actual coefficient-product pairing is R-bilinear. Corrected F4 to group homomorphisms and step 2.1 to define multiplication through that additive map; the explicit formula directly proves R-bilinearity, associativity and the unit. No tensor-module linearity is needed.

F3 incorrectly asserts linearity for every balanced map; b(x,y)=conjugate(x_1*y_2) over C is a counterexample. This is nonfatal to the stated example because its B is explicitly k-bilinear. Corrected F3 to the additive universal property and proved scalar compatibility on finite tensor sums in step 2.1, so B induces a linear functional and every presentation contracts to 1. The Example remains byte-identical.

Also aligned F6 with additive functoriality and proved its k-linearity from the elementary-tensor scalar action.

downstream_reviews.affected_use: Definition coefficient ring and universal parameters, F2 and steps 1.2/1.5 use the finite Laurent ring and unit substitution. Its finite Coxeter matrix gives c <= |S| < infinity; all used clauses survive.
exact_consumer_clauses: **Coefficient ring.** Put $R:=\mathbb Z[v_1^{\pm1},\dots,v_c^{\pm1}]=\Lambda_{\mathbb Z,c}$, the Laurent polynomial ring in $c$ variables ([[lem-hh-finite-polynomial-and-localization-constructions]], part 2): a commutative ring in which every $v_i$ is a unit. Identify the classes with $\{1,\dots,c\}$ and put $v_s:=v_{[s]}\in R^\times$ for $s\in S$.

**Universal parameters.** For every commutative ring $A$ and units $u_1,\dots,u_c\in A^\times$ the assignment $v_i\mapsto u_i$ extends uniquely to a ring homomorphism $R\to A$ ([[lem-hh-finite-polynomial-and-localization-constructions]], part 2); via the universal property of $H$ this makes $R$ the universal coefficient ring for a unit-valued parameter that is constant on each class $[s]$.

[F2] The integers form a commutative ring ([[thm-int-comm-ring]]). The Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_{R,c}$ is a commutative $R$-algebra with monomials $x^\alpha$ ($\alpha\in\mathbb Z^c$) as an $R$-basis, in which each $x_i$ is a unit, and for every commutative $R$-algebra $A$ and units $u_1,\dots,u_c\in A^\times$ there is a unique $R$-algebra homomorphism $\Lambda_{R,c}\to A$ with $x_i\mapsto u_i$. ([[lem-hh-finite-polynomial-and-localization-constructions]])

exact_consumer_clauses: 3. **Bar operator.** The assignment $v_i\mapsto v_i^{-1}$ defines an involutive ring automorphism $\bar{\;}:R\to R$ ([[lem-hh-finite-polynomial-and-localization-constructions]], part 2); there is a unique ring homomorphism $\bar{\;}:H\to H$ which is semilinear over it (i.e. $\overline{rh}=\bar r\,\bar h$) and satisfies $\overline{T_s}=T_s^{-1}$ for all $s\in S$. It is involutive, and $\overline{T_w}=T_{w^{-1}}^{-1}$ for all $w\in W$.

[F5] The Laurent ring $R=\Lambda_{\mathbb Z,c}$ of [[lem-hh-finite-polynomial-and-localization-constructions]], part 2 has the universal property that a choice of units $u_1,\dots,u_c$ in a commutative ring $A$ extends uniquely to a ring homomorphism $R\to A$ with $v_i\mapsto u_i$; applied with $A=R$ and $u_i=v_i$, this says the identity is the only ring endomorphism of $R$ fixing every $v_i$. ([[lem-hh-finite-polynomial-and-localization-constructions]])

([[lem-hh-finite-polynomial-and-localization-constructions]], part 2)

exact_consumer_clauses: [F5] The integers are a commutative ring ([[thm-int-comm-ring]]) with no zero divisors ([[lem-int-cancellation]]), and $0\ne1$ by injectivity of the natural-number embedding ([[lem-nat-embeds-int]]), hence an integral domain. The Laurent polynomial ring in finitely many variables over an integral domain is an integral domain; in an integral domain a product is zero only if one factor is zero. The independent formal variables $v_s,v_t$ in $\mathbb Z[v_s^{\pm1},v_t^{\pm1}]$ do not satisfy either factor equation; the two alternatives describe unit-valued specializations into integral domains. ([[lem-hh-finite-polynomial-and-localization-constructions]])
